Protein synthesis in this patient’s cells is inhibited due to the inhibition of ADP-ribosylation of elongation factor. Which of the following is the donor of ADP-ribose for ADP-ribosylation reactions?
questions.solutionHtml:
Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide

ADP-ribosylation

  • NAD+ acts as the source of ADP-ribose.
  • Different bacterial toxins affect the ADP ribosylation of different proteins as shown below.

 





Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 418, 542

questions.stem: Genetic code is the sum of all the codons which code for the amino acids in the proteins of a given organism. All the following are salient features of the genetic code, EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml:
Punctuated

Salient features of genetic code:

  • Degeneracy: Each amino acid has more than 1 codon
  • Unambiguous: each codon is specific for its amino acid e.g. AUG will always code for methionine
  • Non-overlapping and Comma less: means that the codon is read from a fixed starting point as a continuous sequence of bases, taking three at a time, without any punctuation between codons. e.g. AUCGGGACUGCA will be read as AUC GGG ACU GCA
  • 4. Universal: genetic code has been well conserved during evolution with only slight differences



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 405

questions.stem: A mutation in a gene has caused the insertion of a nonsense codon in the corresponding protein. If this is caused by a single nucleotide change, the original codon may have coded for which one of the following amino acids?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tryptophan
  • A nonsense codon is the conversion of a codon to a stop codon.
  • The stop codons are UGA, UAG, and UAA.
  • The codon for Trp is UGG, which can be converted to UGA or UAG with a single nucleotide change.
  • None of the other amino acid codons, with a single nucleotide change, can be converted into a stop codon.
  • Consult the genetic code below for more understanding:




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd edition Page No. 405

questions.stem: Assume 4 nucleotides code for an amino acid. What is the number of amino acids coded possible?
questions.solutionHtml:
256

This question assumes:

  • 1 nucleotide code→ 4 amino acids
  • 2 nucleotide code → 4 x 4 = 16 amino acids
  • 3 nucleotide code → 4 x 4 x 4= 64 amino acids
  • 4 nucleotide code → 4 x 4 x 4 x 4 = 256 amino acids



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 405

questions.stem: All of the following are synonymous codon pairs EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml:
AUG & AUA

Synonymous codons

  • Codons that specify the same amino acids.
  • g. GGA, GGG, GGU, and GGC codes for glycine
  • Methionine is coded by AUG only. So, there is no synonymous codon for methionine.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 405

questions.stem: What sequence on the template strand of DNA corresponds to the first amino acid inserted into a protein?
questions.solutionHtml:
3' TAC 5'
  • 3' TAC 5' corresponds to the first amino acid inserted into a protein
  • AUG is the codon for the 1st amino acid

Template strand

  • Strand of DNA which is being copied by the RNA polymerase.
  • So, it will be complementary to the AUG.
  • The complementary sequence of AUG is 3' TAC 5' hence the answer.
  • Also, DNA does not contain Uracil. Thus options B, C, and D can be easily ruled out.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 410

questions.stem: Post-translational modification (PTM) refers to the covalent modification of amino acid residues of proteins following protein biosynthesis and is useful for enhancing the chemical functionality of a protein. Which of the following is an example of PTM?
questions.solutionHtml:
Proline to Hydroxyproline
  • Proline has its own codons, hydroxy proline does not. Hydroxyproline is formed from proline by post-translational modification.
  • Glutamate to glutamine is a mutation, not post-translational modification.
  • The same is true for options C and D.

questions.stem: During eukaryotic protein synthesis, phosphorylation of which of the following is enhanced by insulin?
questions.solutionHtml:
eIF4G
  • Insulin phosphorylates both 4E-binding protein and eIF-4G.
  • The 4F complex consists of eIF-4E (4E), eIF-4A, and eIF-4G.
  • 4E is inactive when bound by one of a family of binding proteins (4E-BPs).
  • Insulin and mitogenic growth polypeptides, or growth factors activate the PI3 kinase/AKT kinase pathways, which activate the mTOR kinase, and result in the phosphorylation of 4E-BP. Phosphorylated 4E-BP dissociates from 4E, and the latter is then able to form the 4F complex and bind to the mRNA cap.




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 413

questions.stem: Which of the following statement regarding mutation is wrong?

options.label: A
options.text: Mutations within the exon can be detrimental and mutation in introns will not change the protein

options.label: B
options.text: Mutation of the TATA box markedly reduces the transcription

options.label: C
options.text: A change of purine by a pyrimidine is known as a transition

options.label: D
options.text: Silent mutation does not lead to a change in amino acid

questions.answerText: A change of purine by a pyrimidine is known as a transition
questions.solutionHtml:
A change of purine by a pyrimidine is known as a transition
  • Single-base changes (point mutations) may be
    • transitions
    • transversions.

Transition

Transversions

●        Given pyrimidine is changed to the other pyrimidine or

●        Given purine is changed to the other purine

●        Purine to either of the two pyrimidines or

●        Pyrimidine into either of the two purines

Introns

  • Intervening sequences, present in between exons.
  • Transcribed but not translated.
  • Mutation in introns will not reach the protein.
  • But a mutation in the exon will alter the protein.

Silent mutation

Non-sense mutation

Mis-sense mutation

Amino acid is not changed

The amino acid codon is replaced by a stop codon.

Amino acid is replaced by another amino acid.

TATA box is an important part of transcription initiation machinery and any mutation in this will lead to a lowering of transcription due to inefficient transcription initiation.




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 407-409

questions.stem: Termination of protein translation is caused by all EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml:
48S initiation complex

48S ribosome complex is involved in the initiation of translation, not termination.

Termination of translation:

  • Stop codons are UAA, UAG & UGA, which do not code for any amino acid.
  • Peptidyl transferase is responsible for the release of the polypeptide chain from the P-site of the ribosome.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 414-415

questions.stem: The mutation of a normal codon to a stop codon in DNA often leads to harmful conditions. If a mutation in DNA caused a stop codon TAG to be created on the coding strand between the TATA box and the transcription initiation site, what would be the most likely outcome?
questions.solutionHtml:
No effect
  • There is no coding sequence between the TATA box (the promoter region where RNA polymerase binds) and the transcription initiation site, so the presence of a TAG in the DNA will not affect protein synthesis.
  • In fact, the RNA containing UAG in its sequence will not even be synthesized because the transcription initiation site occurs after this sequence in the DNA.
  • The introns and exons are not affected by this mutation, and splicing will occur normally.
  • Thus, the mRNA produced would be of normal size and would produce a normal-sized protein.




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 387

questions.stem: A pharmaceutical company is studying a new antibiotic that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis. When this antibiotic is added to an in-vitro protein synthesis system that is translating the mRNA sequence AUGUUUUUUUAG, the only product formed is the dipeptide fMet-Phe. What step in protein synthesis is most likely inhibited by the antibiotic?

options.label: B
options.text: Binding of charged tRNA to the ribosomal A site

questions.solutionHtml:
Ribosomal Translocation
  • Because fMet-Phe is made, the ribosomes must be able to complete initiation,
  • Bind Phe-tRNA to the A site and use peptidyltransferase activity to form the first peptide bond.
  • Because the ribosome is not able to proceed any further, ribosomal movement (translocation) is most likely the inhibited step.
  • The ribosome is, therefore, frozen before it reaches the termination codon of this message.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 420-423

questions.stem: Which of the following binds mRNA with the ribosome in prokaryotes?
questions.solutionHtml:
Shine Dalgarno sequence

    • Only in prokaryotes
    • present at -10 position on mRNA,
    • Rich in purines.
    • SD sequence is complementary to 16 s rRNA,
    • Their binding helps in the binding of mRNA with ribosomes during the initiation of translation
  • In eukaryotic cells, ribosomes recognize most eukaryotic mRNAs by binding to the 7-methylguanosine cap at their 5´ terminus.




Textbook of Medical Biochemistry by Dinesh Puri 3rd Edition Page No. 482

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct sequence of the severity of damage for a mutation in DNA?
questions.solutionHtml:
Frameshift> Nonsense > Missense
  • Frameshift mutation is the deletion or insertion of a number of nucleotides not divisible by 3, resulting in misleading of all nucleotides downstream causing a change of a large number of amino acids which is highly detrimental to the function of that protein.
  • Nonsense mutation means a change of a codon with a stop codon (UAA, UAG, UGA). This leads to premature termination of Protein synthesis and a truncated protein which can still function if the place of mutation is near the C-terminus of the protein i.e. if the truncated protein is similar in size to the original protein.
  • Missense mutation means a codon is replaced by another codon, coding for a different amino acid giving rise to a protein with similar properties as the original non-mutated protein.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 407-409

questions.stem: Anticodon 5’-I-G-C-3’ can recognize all of the following codons EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml:
GCG
  • To answer this question, let's understand the wobbling rules in more detail.
  • The figure below is key to understanding the concept.
  • Wobble position is the 3rd position of the codon on mRNA and the first position of anticodon on tRNA in the 5’ to 3’ direction (see fig below).
  • Bases in the wobble position are wobble bases.
  • Wobble bases can base pair via non-Watson Crick base pairing (Watson Crick base pairing is: A only pair with T and G with C).
  • Let’s find the wobble base of the tRNA in the question. The first base (5'-3' direction) of the anticodon is Inosine (I). Thus, it is the wobble base of tRNA here.
  • Inosine (I) in the wobble base can base pair with C, A, or U but not with G.
  • So, the codons it can recognize or pair with are GCC, GCA, and GCU but not GCG.
  • Hence, the answer is option B.




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 407

questions.stem: A tRNA molecule that carries cysteine (tRNAcys) is mischarged. So that it actually carries alanine (ala-tRNAcys). Assuming no correction occurs, what will be the fate of this alanine residue during protein synthesis?

options.label: A
options.text: It will be incorporated into a protein in response to an alanine codon

options.label: B
options.text: It will be incorporated into a protein in response to a cysteine codon

options.label: C
options.text: It will remain attached to the tRNA as it cannot be used for protein synthesis

options.label: D
options.text: It will be chemically converted to cysteine by cellular-enzymes

questions.answerText: It will be incorporated into a protein in response to a cysteine codon
questions.solutionHtml:
It will be incorporated into a protein in response to a cysteine codon

Aminoacyl tRNA synthetase

  • Enzyme attaches amino acid & tRNA and this step is the only proofreading step in translation.
  • If the wrong amino acid gets attached during this step, then it can be corrected but if the correction will not occur in this step, then this wrong amino acid will be added to the protein.
  • tRNAcys is usually recognized by the aminoacyl tRNA synthetase for cysteine and charged with Cysteine to produce cystRNAcys.
  • As per the question, Alanine is incorporated into the tRNAcys to produce alatRNAcys.
  • Ribosomal machinery can’t detect the amino acid attached to the tRNA.
  • Interaction between the codon of mRNA and anticodon of tRNA determines the amino acid incorporated in the polypeptide chain.
  • Anticodon of alatRNAcys interacts with the codon of Cysteine only. So Alanine will be incorporated into the polypeptide in place of Cysteine.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 406

questions.stem: The hydrolytic step leading to the release of a polypeptide chain from a ribosome is catalyzed by which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Peptidyl transferase
  • Peptidyl transferase is responsible for the release of peptidyl chain from a ribosome
  • The release is not done by releasing factor,

During the termination of translation, we have releasing factors:

  • In prokaryotes – RF 1 2 3
  • Eukaryotes – eRF
  • Releasing factor (misnomer) – it can only recognize the stop codon
  • Hence, the hydrolytic step leading to the release of a polypeptide chain from a ribosome is catalyzed by Peptidyl transferase (not by releasing factors).



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 414-415

questions.stem: A therapeutic protein was synthesized by expressing a gene from a plant in E. coli using genetic engineering techniques. It was later observed that Codon no 302 UAG present at the end of the gene is replaced by UGA due to an error in PCR. This will cause what type of mutation in this protein?

options.label: D
options.text: Given information is not sufficient to identify

questions.solutionHtml:
Silent
  • In this mutation, the stop codon – UAG is replaced by another stop codon- UAA. So, this is a silent In silent mutations, there is no change in the primary structure of the protein.
  • Silent Mutation: The codon containing the changed base codes for the same amino acid. For example, if the serine (Ser) codon UCA is given a different third base, U, to become UCU, it still codes for Ser. This is termed a “silent” mutation. This mutation occurs as the codon is degenerate i.e one amino acid can be coded by more than one codon.
  • Missense Mutation: The codon containing the changed base codes for the different amino acids. For example, if the Ser codon UCA is given a different first base, C, to become CCA, it will code for a different amino acid (in this case, proline [Pro]). This is called a “missense” mutation.
  • Nonsense Mutation: The codon containing the changed base becomes a termination codon. For example, if the Ser codon UCA is given a different second base, A, to become UAA, the new codon causes termination of translation at that point and the production of a shortened (truncated) protein.




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 407-409

questions.stem: Which of the following gene sequence (coding region) could produce a protein that contains 200 amino acids and has a phenylalanine residue near its N-terminus? The phenylalanine codons (5′-to-3′) are UUU and UUC.
questions.solutionHtml:
5′-CCATGCCATTTGCATCA -3′
  • In order to answer this question, one first needs to find the start codon: AUG in mRNA and ATG in DNA. Bases 3 to 5 in all first three sequences contain this element. So options d and e are excluded
  • Next, the sequence needs to specify a phenylalanine residue near the amino terminus, which is UUU or UUC in mRNA, or TTT or TTG in DNA, but these sequences need to be in frame with the initiating methionine codon. This condition is satisfied in options a and b. So, option c is excluded
  • The last element to look for is the absence of a premature stop codon because this protein is 300 amino acids long. There should be no stop sequence in the remaining bases of the required piece of DNA.
  • For option b, the last three bases of this sequence are TGA, which in mRNA would be UGA, and this is an in-frame stop signal. So, this sequence would not give rise to a protein that contained 300 amino acids.
  • But in option a there is no premature stop codon and hence it is the answer.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 405

questions.stem: Aminoacyl tRNA synthetase is required for all except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Hydroxyproline
  • Some proteins contain additional amino acids that arise due to post-translational modification of existing amino acyl residues.

Examples:

  • Vitamin C mediated hydroxylation of proline and peptidyl lysine to 4-hydroxyproline and 5-hydroxylysine
  • Vitamin K mediated γ-carboxylation of glutamate
  • Methylation
  • Formylation
  • Acetylation
  • Prenylation (addition of fatty acid residues)
  • Glypiation (addition of Glycosyl PI anchor)
  • Phosphorylation

Therefore Aminoacyl tRNA synthetase is not required by these.




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 43-44

questions.stem: Which amino acid does not include post-translational modification?
questions.solutionHtml:
Selenocysteine
  • Selenocysteine (21st amino acid) & Pyrrolysine (22nd amino acid)
    • Formed by co-translational modification
    • Not by post-translational modifications.

Selenocysteine and Pyrrolysine

●        21st amino acid→Selenocysteine→ UGA

●        22nd amino acid → Pyrrolysine → UAG

●        Both UGA, and UAG are stop codons but co-translational modification can give rise to amino acid selenocysteine and pyrrolysine. co-translational modification.

●        Enzymes that use selenocysteine as their active sites are called Seleno Proteins.

●        Selenocysteine-containing proteins:

●        Glutathione peroxidase

●        Thioredoxin reductase

●        selenoprotein P

●        5’ deiodinases




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 278

questions.stem: A patient suffering from severe pain throughout his body was brought to the hospital. He regularly had such episodes in the last few years. The pain starts with vigorous exercising. Blood analysis showed a reduced blood cell count (anemia), and elongated red blood cells rather than concave. He was diagnosed with Sickle cell anemia. The type of mutation seen in sickle cell anemia is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Point

Sickle-cell anemia

  • Occur due to a single base alteration also known as Point mutation
  • Glutamate at the 6th position of the β-chain of hemoglobin is replaced by Valine due to the creation of valine codon (GTG) for glutamate codon (GAG) by change of base A to T.
  • The abnormal hemoglobin causes red blood cells to become rigid, sticky, and mis-shapen.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 408
